pl-l4d43c1-d1e115.summary: Turns finally to the condition of the resurrection and the manner of those rising, and briefly to the nature of judgment and mercy.

pl-l4d43c1-d1e118.summary: Admits he cannot answer all questions usually raised here, but no Christian should in any way doubt that the flesh of all who have been and will be born, and have died and will die, will rise.
claims: The resurrection of all flesh is certain.
Not all questions about it can be answered.

pl-l4d43c1-d1e124.summary: Cites Isaiah: the dead will rise, and those in the tombs will rise.

pl-l4d43c1-d1e131.summary: Cites Paul: we would not have you ignorant about those asleep, that you not grieve like those without hope; we who are alive will not precede those who sleep, since the Lord will descend from heaven at the command, the archangel's voice, and God's trumpet, the dead in Christ will rise first, and we who remain will be caught up with them in the clouds to meet Christ, and so be with the Lord forever.
claims: The dead rise first, then the living are caught up.

pl-l4d43c1-d1e146.summary: Concludes that these words clearly show the truth of the resurrection and the cause and order of those rising.

pl-l4d43c1.summary: Turns finally to the resurrection, the manner of those rising, and the nature of judgment and mercy. Lombard cannot answer every question, but no Christian should doubt that the flesh of all who have been born and died will rise, as Isaiah says and Paul teaches in 1 Thessalonians: the Lord will descend at the archangel's voice and God's trumpet, the dead in Christ will rise first, and the living will be caught up to meet him, showing the truth, cause, and order of the resurrection.
claims: The flesh of all who have lived will rise.
Paul's account in 1 Thessalonians shows the truth, cause, and order of resurrection.
